description: Gadget-4 built-in SubLink merger tree (FOF+Subfind / SUBFIND_HBT halo finder), HDF5 output produced by restartflag=8. All halos stored in a single flat /TreeHalos array; tree boundaries encoded in /TreeTable (StartOffset, Length). TreeDescendant values are TREE-LOCAL offsets into each tree's own halo slice.
references: Springel et al. (2021), MNRAS 506 2871 — Gadget-4 code paper

Descendant.source_units: tree-local index (int32, values in [0, Length) or -1)
Descendant.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
Descendant.notes: TreeDescendant stores a tree-local index (offset within the tree's own halo slice), NOT a global flat-array index. No offset subtraction is needed. After sorting halos within the tree the index is remapped through the sort permutation. Same-snapshot desc links (Gadget-4 records intra-snapshot FOF mergers this way) are resolved iteratively (up to 10 hops) to produce strictly forward-in-time pointers.

FirstProgenitor.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
FirstProgenitor.notes: Reconstructed by inverting Descendant. TreeHalos/TreeFirstProgenitor is DISCARDED — it points forward in time in Gadget-4 (opposite to SAGE convention) and may contain cross-tree references.

NextProgenitor.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
NextProgenitor.notes: Reconstructed by inverting Descendant. TreeHalos/TreeNextProgenitor is DISCARDED for the same reason as TreeFirstProgenitor.

FirstHaloInFOFGroup.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
FirstHaloInFOFGroup.notes: Reconstructed from (SnapNum, GroupNr) grouping. The FOF central is the halo with the smallest SubhaloNr in each group (Subfind binding-rank order; verified to match TreeFirstHaloInFOFgroup on every group of the gadget4-dust reference). TreeHalos/TreeFirstHaloInFOFgroup is DISCARDED for pointer reconstruction because it carries cross-tree pointers, but min(SubhaloNr) recovers the same central.

NextHaloInFOFGroup.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
NextHaloInFOFGroup.notes: Reconstructed from (SnapNum, GroupNr) grouping. The central (min SubhaloNr) heads the chain and satellites follow by descending SubhaloLen: central -> sat1 -> ... -> -1. Central-first matters because SAGE's satellite iterator starts at Halo[central].NextHaloInFOFGroup. TreeHalos/TreeNextHaloInFOFgroup is DISCARDED for the same reason as TreeFirstHaloInFOFgroup.

Group_M_Crit200.notes: FOF group M200c (mass within R_200_crit). Gadget-4 sets this non-zero only on FOF centrals (SubRankInGr==0); all satellite subhalos are initialised to 0 in halotrees.cc. The driver broadcasts the central's value to all satellites in the same (SnapNum, GroupNr) group so the output field is semantically correct. SAGE ignores this field for satellites anyway (get_virial_mass() in model_misc.c falls through to Len×PartMass for non-central halos), so the propagation has no effect on SAGE physics. UnitMass_in_g=1.989e43 (10^10 Msun) with comoving h-factor included.

Group_M_Mean200.notes: Not available in Gadget-4 built-in tree output. Using sentinel value 0.0.

Group_M_TopHat200.notes: Not available in Gadget-4 built-in tree output. Using sentinel value 0.0.

SubhaloPos.notes: Gadget-4 UnitLength_in_cm=3.0857e24 (1 Mpc). Positions stored in comoving Mpc/h. SAGE schema requires kpc/h on disk; the HDF5 reader multiplies by 0.001 internally (kpc/h → Mpc/h). Shape (N, 3).

SubhaloVel.notes: Peculiar velocity. Gadget-4 UnitVelocity_in_cm_per_s=1e5 (km/s). Direct copy. Shape (N, 3).

SubhaloVelDisp.notes: 1D velocity dispersion. Available in this format; direct copy.

SubhaloVMax.notes: Maximum circular velocity max(sqrt(GM(<r>)/r)). Field name uses lowercase 'max' in Gadget-4. Direct copy.

SubhaloSpin.notes: Specific angular momentum vector [Jx, Jy, Jz] per unit mass — NOT the dimensionless spin parameter lambda. Gadget-4 stores in (Mpc/h)(km/s) = UnitLength * UnitVelocity. SAGE schema requires (kpc/h)(km/s) on disk; the HDF5 reader multiplies by 0.001 internally. Shape (N, 3).

SubhaloIDMostBound.notes: Field name uses lowercase 'b' in Gadget-4 vs uppercase 'B' in SAGE. Dtype is uint32 in source; cast to int64 on write. All uint32 values fit safely in int64.

SnapNum.notes: Zero-based. SnapNum=0 is z~127 (earliest), SnapNum=127 is z~0 (root). Direct copy.

FileNr.notes: Not available; this dataset uses a single merged tree file. Using sentinel value -1.

pointer_logic.description: Gadget-4 stores all halos in a single flat /TreeHalos array. /TreeTable provides StartOffset and Length for each tree. CRITICAL: TreeDescendant values are TREE-LOCAL indices (in [0, Length) or -1), NOT global flat-array indices. No offset subtraction is needed or correct. The five native pointer fields (TreeFirstProgenitor, TreeNextProgenitor, TreeFirstHaloInFOFgroup, TreeNextHaloInFOFgroup, TreeDescendant) are processed as follows: TreeDescendant is used directly; the other four are DISCARDED and reconstructed from scratch.
pointer_logic.Descendant: Load TreeHalos/TreeDescendant[start:start+n] directly — values are already tree-local [0, n) or -1. Clamp out-of-range values to -1 (defensive). Resolve same-snapshot links iteratively (up to 10 hops) using the original desc values for each hop to satisfy SAGE's strict forward-in-time requirement. After sorting halos within the tree (SnapNum desc, SubhaloLen desc), remap all tree-local indices through the sort permutation inverse.
pointer_logic.FirstProgenitor: DISCARD TreeHalos/TreeFirstProgenitor. Reconstruct by inverting the resolved Descendant array: for each halo i that has a valid Descendant d, record i as a progenitor of d. Sort progenitors of the same descendant by SubhaloLen descending; the most massive is FirstProgenitor[d]. Fully vectorised via lexsort, O(N log N).
pointer_logic.NextProgenitor: DISCARD TreeHalos/TreeNextProgenitor. Reconstruct alongside FirstProgenitor: the second-most-massive progenitor of d becomes NextProgenitor[FirstProgenitor[d]], and so on, forming the sibling chain.
pointer_logic.FirstHaloInFOFGroup: DISCARD TreeHalos/TreeFirstHaloInFOFgroup (contains cross-tree pointers). Reconstruct from (SnapNum, GroupNr): sort halos by (SnapNum, GroupNr, -SubhaloLen); the most massive halo in each (SnapNum, GroupNr) group is the central. FirstHaloInFOFGroup[i] = index of central in i's group. Fully vectorised via lexsort + cumsum, O(N log N).
pointer_logic.NextHaloInFOFGroup: DISCARD TreeHalos/TreeNextHaloInFOFgroup. Reconstruct alongside FirstHaloInFOFGroup: consecutive members of the same (SnapNum, GroupNr) group form the satellite chain via NextHaloInFOFGroup.

known_caveats: CRITICAL — TreeDescendant is tree-local, not global: values are offsets into each tree's own halo slice ([0, Length) or -1). Do NOT subtract StartOffset from TreeDescendant. The mistake is easy because Tree0 has StartOffset=0, making global and local interpretations identical for that tree only.

Same-snapshot TreeDescendant: Gadget-4 uses same-snapshot desc to record intra-snapshot FOF mergers (~0.2% of halos). These violate SAGE's strict forward-in-time Descendant requirement and must be resolved by following the chain forward until a cross-snapshot hop or -1 is reached.
TreeFirstProgenitor and TreeNextProgenitor are forward-in-time pointers (Gadget-4 convention opposite to SAGE). They are discarded and reconstructed from TreeDescendant.
TreeFirstHaloInFOFgroup and TreeNextHaloInFOFgroup contain cross-tree pointers and cannot be used directly. They are discarded and reconstructed from (SnapNum, GroupNr) grouping.

UnitLength_in_cm=3.0857e24 means the internal length unit is 1 Mpc (not 1 kpc). SubhaloPos is therefore in comoving Mpc/h and SubhaloSpin in (Mpc/h)(km/s). Both fields require ×1000 scaling before writing.

Group_M_Crit200 is an FOF group property set non-zero only on the FOF central (SubRankInGr==0); all satellite entries are 0 in the raw Gadget-4 output. The driver broadcasts the central's M200c to all satellites in the same (SnapNum, GroupNr) group before writing. SAGE's get_virial_mass() already ignores this field for satellites (uses Len×PartMass), so the propagation is purely for output correctness and does not affect SAGE runs.
Group_M_Mean200 and Group_M_TopHat200 are not present in Gadget-4 built-in tree output; sentinel 0.0 is written for both.
SubhaloIDMostbound is stored as uint32 in Gadget-4 vs the int64 expected by SAGE; an explicit cast is required.
Config shows both SUBFIND and SUBFIND_HBT enabled; SUBFIND_HBT is the active finder. Field names are identical to standard SUBFIND output.
SubhaloHalfmassRad, SubhaloVmaxRad, TreeFirstDescendant, TreeNextDescendant, TreeMainProgenitor, and TreeProgenitor are present in the source but not mapped to any SAGE field.

TreeHalos has NO SubRankInGr field, so the FOF central is identified as the smallest-SubhaloNr halo in each (SnapNum, GroupNr) group. A Gadget-4 TreeTable entry is effectively a forest and routinely contains many independent FOF groups at z=0 (e.g. >1000 in large entries); these are kept as independent Type-0 centrals (the natural L-Halo interpretation), not merged. fix_flybys-style merging is a Consistent-Trees concept and is not applied here.

I/O: the driver caches the /TreeHalos dataset handles once and reads consecutive trees in bounded ~128 MB bulk windows, slicing each tree out of memory instead of issuing a per-tree hyperslab read for every field. Output is byte-identical to per-tree reads; this is a throughput optimisation only.
